articles.title: RBI flags widening inflation risks, puts rate cuts on ice
articles.desc: RBI's Monetary Policy Committee raised the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to address rising inflation concerns. Governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated a generalisation of inflation, with many commodities exceeding 4% inflation. Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta highlighted the influence of external supply-side shocks on inflation projections. External members expressed concerns about the implications of an aggressive rate hike on economic growth.

articles.title: Critical tech list under review to push self-reliance
articles.desc: India's Niti Aayog is preparing a list of critical technologies for enhancing self-reliance and investment. This initiative aims to protect against disruptions due to limited access to essential technologies. Potential technologies include 6G, defence equipment, and electric vehicle powertrains. The government seeks to encourage innovation through the Anusandhan National Research Foundation and other funds. A comprehensive roadmap is expected to be finalized and released next month.

articles.title: Core output grows at series high of 7.9% in Sept
articles.desc: India's core sector output growth for September recorded a remarkable 7.9%, driven largely by expansion in coal and electricity. Notably, refinery products and iron ore also contributed to this growth, supported by a favorable base effect. Coal production saw a sharp rebound with a growth rate of 10.7% following previous negative trends. Electricity generation growth declined slightly, impacted by heatwave conditions in the country.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal to explore trade, investment avenues in Germany & Netherlands
articles.desc: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal is set to visit Germany and the Netherlands for trade engagements. He will participate in the Berlin Global Dialogue and meet various government officials in Germany. The focus will be on technological cooperation, clean technology, and the India-EU FTA negotiations. In the Netherlands, Goyal will hold ministerial meetings to explore expanded trade channels and green transition initiatives.

articles.title: OpenAI president urges AI safeguards as group he funds opposes regulation
articles.desc: OpenAI's safety practices have been in the spotlight in recent months, after the company said a swarm of its AI agents escaped containment and hacked into the AI platform Hugging Face. OpenAI President Greg Brockman was among the group of six tech executives who later signed US President Donald Trump's voluntary AI safety agreement on behalf of their companies, agreeing to work with "independent auditors" and to ensure their AI tools do not "hack or access technical systems in unintended ways."

articles.title: Europe's financial regulators query Google over cloud outage that hit banks
articles.desc: The European Banking Authority said that it has been in contact with Google Cloud to obtain further information on the incident, understand its implications and assess its potential impact on financial entities in the EU, a spokesperson for the watchdog told Reuters.

articles.title: Nvidia's Huang hails Europe's AI potential, flanked by robot ducks
articles.desc: In a demonstration of Europe's AI creativity, Huang shared the stage with tiny duck-shaped, AI-trained robots developed by French startup Pollen Robotics in collaboration with Hugging Face, asking them to perform somersaults.

articles.title: Import window for duty-free raw sugar extended till Dec 31
articles.desc: The government has extended the deadline for duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar to December 31, as domestic imports have lagged at just 3 lakh tonnes due to price control measures. This decision aims to mitigate supply constraints following record high sugar prices linked to reduced domestic production and exports.

articles.title: Meta ordered to pay New Mexico $25 billion after jury finds it deceived Facebook users about privacy
articles.desc: Jurors in September found Meta liable for over 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection laws when a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, harvested Facebook user data to generate targeted political ads for the 2016 election.

articles.title: A warning to anyone with credit card debt...
articles.desc: Martin’s leading this week’s podcast with an urgent warning for anyone carrying credit card: now is the time to act.

articles.title: Burnham proposes plan to cut standing charges from gas bills
articles.desc: The prime minister provided little detail, and there are questions over shifting the fees onto unit costs.

articles.title: Just Eat apologises for AI food mistakes after social media ridicule
articles.desc: A spokesperson said it was removing inaccurate AI images and pausing the rollout of the tool.

articles.title: Vulnerable keys were created but never put to commercial use, investigation on: eMudhra cofounder
articles.desc: eMudhra issues digital signature and website security certificates to enable them securely connect to browsers for public access. "There's no impact to subscribers because we have done all the actions. We are also working with our customers to notify them that there is no impact because no certificates were issued. This does not affect our other lines of business, which is the India digital signature and our enterprise solutions business," eMudhra co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told PTI.

articles.title: Cryptocurrency companies can keep paying interest-like rewards, say federal bank regulators
articles.desc: The new rules are part of the implementation of the GENIUS Act, which was signed into law last year and was meant to codify the rules and regulations around issuers of stablecoins.

articles.title: Explained: What is PHP and why did it take government websites offline?
articles.desc: The developers of PHP said on Wednesday they would release patches for two critical vulnerabilities, and EU cybersecurity officials warned organisations unable to apply the fixes to take affected websites offline. Here is what you need to know:

articles.title: NaBFID gets Finance Ministry, RBI nod for national infrastructure project repository
articles.desc: NaBFID has obtained approvals from the finance ministry and the Reserve Bank of India to establish a national repository. This repository will offer consolidated information on infrastructure projects for lenders and investors. The platform aims to facilitate access to data sourced from various government agencies like NHAI and others. NaBFID is considering partnerships with financial institutions to enhance the repository's effectiveness.

articles.title: EBay to lay off 9% of workforce in push to simplify operations
articles.desc: EBay will lay off about 1,000 employees, representing 9% of its workforce, to streamline operations. The company previously reduced its staff by 800 positions in February to improve efficiency. EBay is focusing on authenticated luxury goods, collectibles, and refurbished products, which have attracted higher-paying consumers. The recent acquisition of fashion resale platform Depop has also strengthened eBay's market position. EBay plans to report its latest earnings next week.

articles.title: Inflation remains top of mind, MPC minutes show
articles.desc: RBI's monetary policy committee has increased the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points due to inflation concerns. Core inflation has shown an upward trajectory, indicating a normalization from earlier benign levels. Various members expressed views on external supply shocks impacting inflation expectations and the need for timely policy adjustments. The differing opinions highlight the complexities of achieving growth while managing inflation effectively.

articles.title: Special team to probe eMudhra incident; impact on Indian websites, applications very limited: Govt
articles.desc: The ministry said the reported security incident pertains to eMudhra’s global certificate business, and its impact on Indian websites is very limited.It also said some social media accounts were indulging in fear-mongering about the impact.

articles.title: Deepinder Goyal’s Temple to open pre-orders on November 1
articles.desc: Temple is a head-worn device that tracks blood flow and oxygenation inside the brain. Goyal, who stepped down as Eternal CEO in February, had said in August that pre-orders for a limited launch edition would open soon.

articles.title: Blinkit sees no compelling case for expanding private labels, says Dhindsa
articles.desc: Albinder Dhindsa, CEO of Eternal, voiced skepticism regarding the potential for private labels to enhance profit margins. He emphasised that effective brand development mandates considerable investment in both marketing and product development, areas where Blinkit falls short.

articles.title: Glance to be integrated by default on Android TVs in US, India, Japan in partnership with Google
articles.desc: Under the collaboration, Glance will transform idle TV screens into interactive shoppable storefronts across fashion, travel, food, wellness, and other lifestyle categories.

articles.title: Extent of rate hike cycle to depend on growth-inflation outlook: RBI Governor
articles.desc: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the duration and extent of the rate hike cycle will be contingent on the actual growth-inflation developments and outlook. The governor and other five Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) members voted to raise the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5 per cent. The rate was hiked after a gap of nearly four years. He noted that there are increasing signs of generalisation of inflation.

articles.title: India wants manufacturing at 25% of GDP — will AI in factories help?
India’s economy stays resilient at 7.1%, but rising inflation raises a red flag, says RBI's Sanjay Malhotra
articles.desc: The Indian economy is projected to maintain a growth rate of 7.1% for the year 2026-27. This projection is an increase from the previously estimated 6.7%. RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra noted that inflationary pressures are rising, which could impact the growth outlook. Despite turbulent global conditions, India's economic resilience has been remarkable according to the governor.

articles.title: Dark Matter: Eternal’s chatbot will keep user conversations private even from the company — Deepinder Goyal
articles.desc: In a letter to shareholders, Goyal explained the idea behind Dark was to remove the worry that someone, someday, can read what you tell an AI bot. “All of us have a dark side, and it needs an outlet where it doesn’t have to hide,” he wrote.

articles.title: New policy in works to boost agrivoltaics in India; enhance farmers' income via energy generation
articles.desc: India's government is formulating a policy to enhance the adoption of agrivoltaics across the country. This initiative aims to increase farmers' income by combining agricultural production with solar energy generation. States with significant agrivoltaic potential include Maharashtra, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh, accounting for nearly half of India's cropland suitable for this practice.

articles.title: India’s infrastructure output jumps 7.9% in September on strong coal, steel growth
articles.desc: The latest numbers from the Indian government show that the country's infrastructure output has jumped by 7.9% compared to last year, as of September. This index measures the activity across nine different sectors, which gives us a good idea of how the economy is doing. It's a positive sign for growth!

articles.title: Einride expands Nvidia partnership to deploy AI reasoning model for self-driving trucks
articles.desc: Self-driving truck company Einride said on Wednesday it would broaden its partnership with Nvidia by testing the chipmaker's AI reasoning model, Alpamayo, in its self-driving vehicles, aiming to speed up the expansion of autonomous freight services while lowering development costs

articles.title: Booking.com targeted in EU investigation into phishing scams, fraudulent listings
articles.desc: The Commission, which is the EU tech and competition enforcer, said it opened an investigation following a preliminary probe and after analysing risk assessment reports submitted by Booking.com this year and the previous three years.

articles.title: India’s growth story needs jobs to match the numbers, says ex-RBI Governor D Subbarao
articles.desc: Former RBI Governor D Subbarao has said India must make economic growth more employment-intensive, warning that rapid output expansion alone cannot deliver a demographic dividend. He called for greater private investment, labour-intensive manufacturing and improved skills, while urging transparent technical scrutiny of GDP estimates and differences with other economic indicators.
